title: Choose the visual world for at-here
question: The roll assigned the Operator's Exchange. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Operator's Exchange
options.lineage: manual telephone exchange jack fields, 1920s to 1950s
options.thesis: Every app is a jack on one panel; the card connects you instead of listing you.
options.viewport: One full-width light enamel panel. The top designation strip carries the handle at engraved title scale with the avatar set in the line-lamp bezel. Below it the jack field: one row per app, each a full-width coloured designation strip with the app name engraved, its record collections on a leader line, a brass jack as the row's only action, and a lit lamp for presence. Two toggle switches at the panel foot: vCard and JSON.
options.risk: Reads as a toy if the jack rows are not ruled strictly enough to scan like a table, and slides into the black-panel-with-glowing-lamps cluster if the enamel goes dark. The panel stays light.

raised.raise: Rows live in fixed columns (strip, evidence, jack, lamp) that never move; a state change restyles the row without breaking the ruling.
Hierarchy by scale contrast alone: the handle is enormous, everything else is engraved small in one face.
Colour commits at region scale: each app's designation strip is a full-width saturated band, never a dot beside grey text.
One orchestrated deploy on load: lamps come up in sequence as the panel resolves, and reduced-motion snaps to the lit state.
Every label carries its evidence: each jack's leader line names the record collections that justify the lamp, so presence is shown, not asserted.

options.label: Finger Printout
options.thesis: The oldest 'where is this person' protocol, reprinted on continuous-feed paper.
options.viewport: A wide sheet with perforated tractor edges. The header block in fixed-width type: Login, Name, Directory (the PDS), Since. Then Plan: one line per app with its URL in ribbon ink, red overstrike for the primary link. The vCard is a tear-off strip at the sheet's foot.
options.risk: Also where most developer-facing tools land; a monospace page is the category-plus-avoidance guess for this audience, and it sits one step from the terminal-dump cliché.

options.label: Split-flap Concourse
options.thesis: The account as a departures board: apps are destinations, rows are ranked, flaps cascade as data lands.
options.viewport: A dark board headed by the handle in fixed flap cells. One row per app: destination (app name), via (profile URL), status (present). Unknown apps sit as unlisted destinations in the last rows.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: apps map to destinations and the board is already a strict scanable table. Holds product clarity, loses audience identification to the telephony world, and lands in the dark-surface cluster.
options.risk: Reads as retro novelty the moment the grid loosens.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.thesis: Cards on a warm ground with one saturated colour that only appears where you can press.
options.viewport: Avatar and name in a header card, then one card per app with the app name, a plain-language line, and a single coloured Open button.
options.case: Fuses trivially and reads instantly. Holds clarity, loses identification because it is the category's default face and indistinguishable from the link-in-bio pages it would sit beside.
options.risk: Nobody remembers it an hour later.

options.label: Variable Type Specimen
options.thesis: The handle as a giant glyph, apps as a specimen grid.
options.viewport: One enormous handle, a grid of glyph-sized app cells, a mono readout.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the audience does not identify with type foundries and an axis slider has no honest product meaning.

options.label: Modular Identity Blocks
options.thesis: Saturated bars and scattered vector marks over the avatar photo.
options.viewport: Avatar photo tilted under a stack of coloured bars, one per app.
options.case: Fuses loosely: the scatter grammar fights an Operate task and the audience does not identify with agency identity work.
options.kept: Colour owns whole regions, never accents.

options.label: Miura-fold Sheet
options.thesis: The card unfolds from a packet into a tessellated field of apps.
options.viewport: A small gold packet that deploys into a parallelogram grid.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a parallelogram grid defeats scanning and the audience has no attachment to aerospace origami.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.thesis: The DID at the core, apps as floating rods held in tension.
options.viewport: A network diagram of rods and cords with force labels on leader lines.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the structure has no honest mapping to apps and the audience does not read force diagrams.
options.kept: Every label carries its evidence on a leader line.

canonCard.label: The link-in-bio page
canonCard.thesis: What this category ships, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Avatar, name, bio, then stacked full-width buttons, one per app.
